solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Insect — member of a foursome, we hear

indicators.note: we hear tells the solver to go by how the word is spoken, not its spelling

parts.note: a Beatle was one of the four members of the Beatles

explanation.surface: Someone describes an insect, then mentions a band member they have heard of.
explanation.walkthrough: 'we hear' marks a sound-alike: BEATLE, one of the famous four, is said just like the insect's name.
explanation.definitionFit: A beetle is an insect with hard wing cases, so the insect class covers it.

clue.text: Support a revolutionary bringing physical pain

parts.note: to back means to support
Che Guevara was a revolutionary

explanation.surface: Supporting a revolutionary cause brings bodily suffering.
explanation.definitionFit: Backache is an ache in the back, a kind of bodily pain.

clue.text: Some alert — nasty material

indicators.note: nasty suggests something messed up, so these letters are thrown into a new order

explanation.surface: A warning about some nasty material.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Some' looks like a hidden-word signal, but it is fodder: SOME and ALERT are mixed up by 'nasty'.
explanation.definitionFit: An elastomer is a rubbery polymer, a stretchy substance used in manufacturing.

clue.text: Policy creating row

definitions.meaning: a ... is a policy, as in the party ...

explanation.surface: A policy leads to a quarrel.
explanation.walkthrough: 'row' tempts as a quarrel; it is a row of things in a line.
explanation.definitionFit: A party line is its policy, and a line of chairs is a row.

clue.text: Is collection of poetry added to record events?

indicators.note: added to says the first pieces are attached after the record, setting the order

parts.note: EP is an extended-play record
odes are poems, so a group of them is a collection of poetry

explanation.surface: A question about whether poetry recited counts as recording events.
explanation.walkthrough: 'added to' sets the order: the record comes first. The question mark flags that episodes are only one kind of event.
explanation.definitionFit: Episodes are incidents or occurrences in a sequence, a type of event, hence the question mark.

clue.text: Leap — it's developed into a system of exercises

indicators.note: developed into says these letters grow into a different arrangement

explanation.surface: A leap has evolved into a whole exercise regime.
explanation.walkthrough: 'developed into' rearranges LEAP and ITS.
explanation.definitionFit: Pilates is a fitness method of controlled movements strengthening the body's core.

clue.text: Low serpent disguised in fern

indicators.note: disguised means the letters are dressed up in a new order

explanation.surface: A snake hides low down in the ferns.
explanation.walkthrough: 'disguised' rearranges LOW and SERPENT.
explanation.definitionFit: Spleenwort is a genus of small ferns, once used to treat the spleen.

clue.text: Woman is at foot of pole, ascending

indicators.note: at foot of puts the word is below the other piece in the column
in a down clue, ascending means the word reads upward, so backwards

parts.note: a rod is a pole

explanation.surface: A woman stands at the base of a pole, about to climb it.
explanation.walkthrough: 'ascending' turns ROD upward to DOR; 'at foot of' puts IS below it.
explanation.definitionFit: Doris is a woman's first name.

clue.text: Pubs ultimately convenient for this?

indicators.note: ultimately points to the final letter of the word pubs

parts.note: handy means convenient

explanation.surface: Asks whether pubs are the obvious handy place to get this drink.
explanation.walkthrough: 'ultimately' takes S from 'Pubs'. The whole clue also describes the answer: pubs serve it.
explanation.definitionFit: Shandy is beer mixed with lemonade, a drink pubs readily serve.

clue.text: Changed climate, ultimately very very dry all around

indicators.note: all around means one piece surrounds the other

parts.note: arid means very dry

indicators.note: ultimately points to the final letter of the word climate

explanation.surface: The climate has changed, now becoming very, very dry everywhere.
explanation.walkthrough: 'ultimately' takes E from 'climate'; 'all around' puts ARID around it.
explanation.definitionFit: Varied as a verb form means altered or modified, so changed.

clue.text: Old-fashioned protection coming with series of letters?

definitions.meaning: medieval armour made of linked rings
a chain of letters sent on, like a chain letter

explanation.surface: Something old-fashioned offers protection when a sequence of letters arrives.
explanation.walkthrough: The second reading splits the answer into CHAIN and MAIL: post passed along in a chain.
explanation.definitionFit: Linked metal-ring armour guarded knights in battle, which is old-fashioned body protection.

clue.text: Life form of particular value

indicators.note: of tells the solver the answer is made of letters taken from within the next words

explanation.surface: A life form described as having a particular value.
explanation.walkthrough: 'of' marks the answer as sitting inside 'particuLAR VAlue'.
explanation.definitionFit: A larva is an immature stage of an insect, a living form before metamorphosis.

clue.text: Group of lecturers with old car

parts.note: AUT is the Association of University Teachers, a former UK lecturers' union

explanation.surface: A group of lecturers turns up with an old car.
explanation.walkthrough: The AUT was a British trade union for university staff, later merged into the UCU.
explanation.definitionFit: Auto is a short informal word for an automobile, especially in American usage.

clue.text: Hell having long hair? It makes one unhappy

parts.note: Dis is the Roman underworld, so hell
tressed means having tresses, long locks of hair

explanation.surface: Someone asks whether hell is having long hair, which certainly makes one unhappy.
explanation.walkthrough: Dis is the classical god and realm of the underworld, a crossword stand-in for hell.
explanation.definitionFit: Distressed means upset or anxious, a close synonym for being unhappy.

clue.text: Likely position of numbers associated with bridge?

definitions.text: position of numbers associated with bridge?
definitions.meaning: the numbers of a bridge hand are printed ...

explanation.surface: Asks where the numbers relating to a bridge are likely to be.
explanation.walkthrough: 'bridge' is the card game, not a span.
explanation.definitionFit: Something on the cards is probable, an idiom from fortune telling.

clue.text: Carrier transporting small human being maybe

indicators.note: a carrier transporting something holds it within, so one piece goes inside the other

parts.note: a hod is a builder's trough for carrying bricks
mini means small

explanation.surface: A carrier is transporting a small human being, perhaps a baby.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Carrier' suggests a pram or ship, but here it is the bricklayer's hod; 'transporting' makes it hold the small piece. 'maybe' shows a human is only one example.
explanation.definitionFit: Hominids are the family of great apes including people, so a human is one example.

clue.text: Was maybe got rid of

parts.note: the word saw, with off as an anagram signal, gives WAS; maybe flags this

explanation.surface: A brief, puzzled query about whether something was got rid of.
explanation.walkthrough: A reverse clue: the answer read as instructions, SAW with 'off' meaning 'rearranged', makes WAS.
explanation.definitionFit: To saw off is to remove by cutting, so it means got rid of a part.

clue.text: Linguistic jumble from signal far off

indicators.note: off means out of order, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A garbled message comes from a signal far away.
explanation.walkthrough: 'off' rearranges SIGNAL and FAR.
explanation.definitionFit: Franglais is French spiced with English words, a mixed-up hybrid language.

clue.text: I am fellow leading hospital department, everywhere present

indicators.note: leading in a down clue means coming ahead of the next piece

parts.note: contracted to I'm
a man is a fellow
ENT is ear, nose and throat

explanation.surface: Someone declares they lead a hospital department and are everywhere.
explanation.definitionFit: Immanent means pervading the world, the theological sense of being present throughout.

clue.text: Plant sheltered by porch ideally

indicators.note: sheltered by says the answer sits inside the following words, kept under cover

explanation.surface: A plant ideally kept under a porch for shelter.
explanation.walkthrough: 'sheltered by' marks the answer as inside 'pORCH IDeally'.
explanation.definitionFit: Orchids are flowering plants prized for their showy blooms.

clue.text: Watery expanse that provides an exceptionally uplifting experience

definitions.text: Watery expanse that provides an exceptionally uplifting experience

parts.words: Watery expanse that provides an exceptionally uplifting experience
parts.note: this salt lake is so salty that bathers float, lifted up by the water

explanation.surface: An inspiring lake trip.
explanation.walkthrough: 'uplifting' sounds emotional but means literally buoyant.
explanation.definitionFit: The salt lake between Israel and Jordan is so dense that swimmers float effortlessly.

clue.text: Female anger when confronting a jolly lethal device

indicators.note: when confronting means standing in front of, so these pieces come before the rest

parts.note: ire means anger
a jolly is old slang for a Royal Marine, RM

explanation.surface: An angry woman faces a cheerful person armed with something lethal.
explanation.walkthrough: 'jolly' is a noun here: naval slang for a Royal Marine, abbreviated RM.
explanation.definitionFit: A firearm is a gun, a weapon that can kill.

clue.text: Bird and flower in Cornwall needing study

parts.note: the Fal is a river in Cornwall, and a river is a flower, something that flows
to con is to study

explanation.surface: A bird and a Cornish flower need study.
explanation.walkthrough: 'flower' is a thing that flows: a river. Cornwall is a county in south-west England.
explanation.definitionFit: A falcon is a bird of prey.

clue.text: One is well

parts.note: the word well is an example of this part of speech

explanation.surface: Someone reports that they are healthy.
explanation.walkthrough: 'well' looks like a health report, but the clue is about grammar.
explanation.definitionFit: Well, as in 'sing well', modifies a verb, which is that word class.

clue.text: Charming lord, ultimately good enough to enter Parliament?

indicators.note: ultimately points to the final letter of the word lord

parts.note: someone electable could win a seat and enter Parliament

explanation.surface: A charming lord who might be good enough to win a seat in Parliament.
explanation.walkthrough: 'ultimately' takes D, the last letter of 'lord'.
explanation.definitionFit: Delectable means delightful or very pleasing, close to charming.

clue.text: Reason officer turned up to grab soldier

indicators.note: to grab means to hold another piece inside
in a down clue, turned up means read upwards, so backwards

parts.note: COL is a colonel
GI is a US soldier

explanation.surface: An officer arrives with a reason to arrest a soldier.
explanation.walkthrough: In a down entry 'turned up' means written bottom to top; 'to grab' makes the officer hold the American soldier.
explanation.definitionFit: Logic is reasoning, the reasoned thinking behind an argument.

clue.text: Exclamation of surprise when meeting a good ruler

indicators.note: when meeting says the pieces join side by side, the exclamation coming after

parts.note: ha is a cry of surprise

explanation.surface: Someone exclaims in surprise on meeting a good ruler.
explanation.walkthrough: The exclamation comes last though it opens the clue.
explanation.definitionFit: An agha is a title for an Ottoman commander or chief, a ruler.

clue.text: German unaffected by rebound?

parts.note: a German name that reads the same when bounced back from end to start

explanation.surface: A German who is unbothered by a rebound.
explanation.walkthrough: The name is a palindrome, so turning it round changes nothing.
explanation.definitionFit: This is a common German man's name that is spelt identically in both directions.

clue.text: Anxious bird abandoning lake and river

indicators.note: the bird abandoning the lake means that letter leaves the bird's name

parts.note: an eagle is a bird

explanation.surface: An anxious bird flies away from the lake and the river.
explanation.walkthrough: 'abandoning' takes L out of EAGLE, leaving EAGE; 'and' then adds R.
explanation.definitionFit: Eager means keen and impatient, the sense of anxious in 'anxious to please'.

clue.text: Means of transmitting brief acknowledgment to crowds?

parts.note: brief means short
a celebrity acknowledges a crowd with a wave

explanation.surface: A quick acknowledgment given to crowds, like a royal greeting.
explanation.definitionFit: Shortwave is a band of radio frequencies used for long-distance broadcasting.

clue.text: Pals, we may deduce, offer congratulatory gesture

parts.note: SLAP put back, reversed, gives PALS

explanation.surface: Friends offer a congratulatory gesture, we may conclude.
explanation.walkthrough: A reverse clue: 'we may deduce' invites working back from the answer, where SLAP read 'back' spells PALS.
explanation.definitionFit: A backslap is a hearty pat on the back to praise someone.

clue.text: My group of pupils getting support

parts.note: cor is an exclamation of surprise, like my!
a set is a class of pupils grouped by ability

explanation.surface: A teacher remarks on a class getting support.
explanation.walkthrough: 'My' is an exclamation, matched by the British 'cor!'; schools in Britain group pupils by ability into sets.
explanation.definitionFit: A corset is a close-fitting undergarment that shapes and holds up the body.
